title: Implement Levenshtein edit distance in Rust
description: Implement levenshtein(a: &str, b: &str) -> usize using dynamic programming (2-row rolling array).

task_spec.prompt:
Implement levenshtein(a, b) in src/lib.rs using DP with a 2-row rolling array:
- Convert a and b to Vec<char>
- Initialize prev row as [0, 1, 2, ..., b.len()]
- For each char in a: init curr[0]=i+1; for each char in b: cost = if a[i]==b[j] {0} else {1}; curr[j+1] = min(curr[j]+1, prev[j+1]+1, prev[j]+cost)
- After each row, swap prev and curr
- Return prev[b.len()]
All 5 tests must pass.
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test --quiet` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test --quiet` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
